AI BUILD DAY · Follow-along Guide

Build a Project Intake system with Asana AI

Today you'll build a fully automated Project Intake system for a PMO team — from scratch. You'll start by asking Dash what needs your attention, then build the machine that handles it: Assistive AI generates the structure, AI Studio rules process every incoming request automatically, and an AI Teammate handles planning on demand.

1
Asana Dash

Ask Dash what needs your attention

Before building anything, start where every workday should start — with Dash, your AI Chief of Staff. Dash knows your goals and priorities and surfaces what needs your attention. Ask it one question and see what it brings back.

Steps

  • Open an incognito browser window and log in to Asana with the demo account you were given
    Note: Incognito keeps the demo account separate from any Asana account you're already signed in to.
  • Click Work with Dash in the top right of your screen (or press Tab + J)
  • Ask Dash the question below
  • Review what Dash surfaces — your tasks, meetings, and anything that needs a decision
  • Notice how requests arrive as unstructured asks. Today you'll build the intake system that turns them into structured, routed work
Ask Dash
What are my responsibilities for today?
2
Assistive AI

Create a playground project

Dash showed you the work heading your way — now let's build the system that handles it. We'll use Asana's Assistive AI to generate a fully structured Project Intake system for a PMO team, all from three prompts. What would typically take hours of manual setup, we're going to do in minutes.

Steps

  • Click Create
  • Select Project
  • Choose "Create with AI"
  • Send the three prompts below one at a time, verifying each step before moving on.
    Note: Do not click the "Go to project" button until Prompt 3 has been fully applied.
Prompt 1 · Create the project
Create a project intake tracker to manage incoming project requests. The project should have 4 sections: Intake, Under Review, Generate Project Presentation, and Initiate Project.
Add emojis at the start of each section name.
Prompt 2 · Add custom fields
Add the following custom fields to this project:
1. Department (multi-select with options: Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, IT, Operations, Product, Legal, Customer Success, Other)
2. Business Impact (text)

*Also, remove the "Untitled section" from the project
Prompt 3 · Add the intake form
Add an intake form to this project with a single field: Project Description (paragraph text). No fields should be mandatory.
3
AI Studio

Auto-update the task title

Now let's set up our first AI Studio rule. As soon as a request lands in Intake, this rule will rename the task to something clear and actionable — so we never have to parse a vague form submission again.

Steps

  • Open your project and click Customize
  • Select Rules → + Add rule
  • Browse suggestions and select "Automatically name tasks"
  • Replace the default prompt with the one below
  • Click Save
  • Copy the Example below and submit it via the intake form
  • Confirm the rule worked correctly
Renaming prompt
Your job is to rename incoming project intake requests. Review the task description, then rename the task to clearly reflect what is being requested. Task names should be short, action-oriented, and include the type of request and the team or department where possible.

[Examples] "New CRM Integration Request — Sales" "Website Redesign Request — Marketing" "Budget Approval Request — Finance"

Example — use this to test

The Product team needs to redesign our customer portal to improve user experience and reduce inbound support tickets. The current interface is five years old and new user onboarding drop-off has increased by 23% over the last two quarters. We have budget approved and are aiming to deliver before our annual customer conference in Q3, making this a large and time-sensitive initiative for the business.

4
AI Studio

Populate fields and move to review

Now we're going to set up a second AI Studio rule that fires as soon as a task is added to the project — automatically identifying the department, writing a business impact statement, populating both custom fields, then moving the request to Under Review and assigning it to a human reviewer. No manual data entry needed — but a person still owns the review.

Steps

  • Open your project and click Customize
  • Select Rules → + Add rule
  • Paste the prompt below into the text box under "What do you want to automate?"
  • Click Publish Rule
  • Copy the Example below and submit it via the intake form
  • Confirm the rule worked correctly
Rule Creation Prompt
When a task is added to this project, please identify the appropriate department from the description—selecting from Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, IT, Operations, Product, Legal, Customer Success, or Other—and set the Department field accordingly. Next, write a concise 1–2 sentence description of the business impact, explaining the problem it solves, opportunity it captures, or risk it mitigates, to populate the Business Impact field. Finally, move the task to the "Under Review" section and assign it to me.

Example — use this to test

The Sales team needs a centralised enablement platform to give reps fast access to up-to-date pitch decks, case studies, and competitive intelligence. Content is currently scattered across shared drives and email threads, and reps are regularly going into customer calls underprepared, which is contributing to a 15% lower win rate compared to last year. This is a medium-sized initiative we want to kick off next quarter with involvement from Marketing and Sales Operations.

5
AI Teammate

Build your AI Teammate

Now we're going to create our AI Teammate — a senior project management expert that lives inside this project, available at any stage to answer questions, provide guidance on scope and priorities, and take action directly on tasks.

Steps

  • Click Create (the red omni-button)
  • Select AI Teammate.
  • Select the Project Manager teammate template from the gallery (under the Essentials category).
  • Click Create AI Teammate.
  • Rename your teammate: [Your Name] Project Manager
    Note: In practice, you'd typically share one AI Teammate across your team rather than create separate ones. Here, everyone builds their own, so please add your name so you can easily find it!
6
AI Teammate

Generate a project plan

This is where the Teammate really shines. We're going to tag it in a comment on the task we already created and ask it to generate a full project plan — broken down into subtasks, right there on the task.

Steps

  • Open the request you submitted earlier
  • Add a comment, tag your Teammate using @, and send the message below
  • Click View activity next to AI Teammates in the comment section to check its activity (verify it includes "Activated skill")
  • Your Teammate will generate a project plan as subtasks on the task
Tag your Teammate in a comment
@Teammate Based on the project description and everything captured on this task, please generate a detailed project plan as subtasks of this task.
7
AI Teammate

Auto-generate a project presentation

Want to take it further? Let's set up a rule that automatically creates a subtask assigned to our Teammate whenever a request moves to Generate Project Presentation. The Teammate will produce a polished HTML presentation ready to share with stakeholders — no manual prompt needed.

Steps

  • Open your project and click Customize
  • Select Rules → + Add rule
  • Select Start from scratch
  • Set the trigger to "Task moved to a section" → Generate Project Presentation
  • Add an action: Create a subtask named "Generate Project Presentation" and assign it to your Teammate
    Note: Leave "Let AI decide the number of subtasks to create" unchecked, and leave AI Instructions blank — it isn't needed for this step.
  • Paste the prompt below as the subtask description
  • Click Publish Rule
  • Move the task to the Generate Project Presentation section to trigger the rule
  • Review the Project Presentation (HTML file) the AI Teammate creates and attaches to the task
Brief generation prompt · subtask description
Generate a Project Presentation

Create a stunning HTML presentation for this project request. Here's exactly what I want:

Design: Clean, modern layout with a dark header, white content sections, and a colour-coded department badge.

Header: Include the project name, department, and today's date.

Sections:
1. Executive Summary — a concise overview of the request
2. Business Impact — why this matters and what problem it solves
3. Key Objectives — the main goals and expected outcomes
4. Scope & Constraints — known boundaries, dependencies, and risks
5. Recommended Next Steps

Footer: Include a note saying this presentation was generated by your AI Teammate.

Output the complete HTML as a single file with all styles included inline. Make it look like something you'd be proud to present to a leadership team.

Bonus Steps

  • Provide the following feedback to the AI Teammate in the task's comment section.
  • Check "Customize > Memory" on the AI Teammate's profile screen.
  • Move another task to the "Generate Project Presentation" section and check the generated HTML.
Feedback to AI Teammate
@Teammate
Going forward, please follow the Recommended Color Palette below:
1. Asana White: #FFFFFF
2. Asana Black: #0B0505
3. Asana Coral: #FF584A
4. Fuchsia: #FD3FFD
5. Light Fuchsia: #FFC9FF
6. Neutral Grey: #F3F3F3
